name: keras_uncompiled
title: Keras click-through classifier fed by a shuffled tf.data holdout
origin: written alongside ANA-7 / ANA-9 to exercise MLV705 and MLV121 (Sprint 4)
tunedWhy: the rules were developed against this project, so its numbers are a ceiling, not a measurement - it is excluded from the unseen headline in ACCURACY.md
note: No `graph` block: this program was added for its findings, and claiming a hand-drawn diagram for it would move the graph-fidelity ratchet on evidence nobody drew.

expected.defect: the take/skip holdout is carved out of a shuffled dataset with reshuffle_each_iteration left at its default
expected.why: tf.data re-draws both halves on every epoch, so by the second pass every validation row has been trained on and the holdout has stopped existing

expected.defect: nothing calls model.compile() anywhere in the project
expected.why: an uncompiled model has no optimizer and no loss, so fit() raises on its first call

forbidden.why: the output layer does carry activation="softmax", but the project constructs no loss at all - an activation on its own is not a contradiction
keras.utils.set_random_seed(1234) seeds TensorFlow, NumPy and Python at line 13
there is no sklearn or torch splitter in this project; take/skip is a tf.data subset, not a SPLIT-role call
Keras model.fit owns the loop - no hand-written gradient update exists here
model.eval() is a torch idiom and model.evaluate() is not an inference-mode bug
